title: Scoped service roles and ephemeral session policies for private deploys
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Deliver a Terraform module and companion CI checks that provide a repeatable pattern for creating scoped service roles, short-lived session policies, and least-privilege bindings for Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to replace ad-hoc role creation in customer onboarding with a tested, auditable, and upgradeable module that: 1) generates narrowly scoped IAM roles for services and operator personas, 2) emits short-lived session policies for ephemeral tasks (deploy runs, bootstrap operations), 3) ships linting and policy templates compatible with our SSO/KMS integrations, and 4) includes a migration/upgrade playbook and health checks for drift and policy regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can create namespaced roles and attach minimal policies for: runtime instances, bootstrap agents, monitoring agents, and CI deployer accounts
Module exposes inputs for scope (env, biz_unit), permission templates (read-only, runtime-write), and external principals (cross-account roles)
Session policy generator produces temporary IAM session specs used by the bootstrapper with expiry defaults and strict conditions (source VPC, MFA, tag-based restrictions)
CI pipeline runs policy linter (tfsec/custom rules) and fails on wildcard actions or overly permissive resources
Upgrade playbook documented with automated dry-run plan and rollback instructions; no manual IAM changes required for minor version bumps
Health checks detect drift (unexpected policy additions) and surface a remediation PR + incident link in the Console
implementation_steps: Design policy templates and minimal permission sets with Security (list S3 buckets, putObject limited to customer buckets, describe EC2, assume role)
Create Terraform module: inputs, outputs, examples/ directory, and strict naming conventions for resources
Add optional iam_policy_document generation utility and map to external principal ARNs
Implement ephemeral session policy generator using external data source and timestamped tags
Wire CI checks: tffmt, tfsec with custom rules, and unit test harness using terratest
Create upgrade playbook and automated plan job in GitHub Actions that runs 'terraform plan' against a cloned state and verifies no destructive changes
Add post-deploy health checks: policy hash snapshots, periodic drift scanner, and dashboard alerts
test_plan: Unit tests for policy generation (terratest) asserting no '*' actions in produced JSON
Integration test that provisions module into a sandbox VPC and verifies role can be assumed and limited actions succeed/fail as expected
Security review checklist completed and signed off by Security team
Load test for ephemeral session creation: create 50 short-lived sessions concurrently to ensure token issuance scales
Manual upgrade test: run major/minor upgrade scenarios following the playbook and validate rollback path
rollout_plan: Stage 1: create module and examples in infra-private repo; run internal sandbox onboarding for infra team
Stage 2: onboard 2 pilot customers (non-sensitive) with dedicated support window; monitor Console and cost/latency telemetry
Stage 3: wider rollout to all new Private deployments and opt-in for existing customers via migration PRs
Stage 4: deprecate legacy ad-hoc role templates after 30 days of zero usage and run automated cleanup with owner approval
upgrade_playbook: Step 0: Read module CHANGELOG and release notes; confirm security_review_required flag state
Step 1: Create branch and run 'terraform plan' in dry-run environment using replicated state
Step 2: CI smoke tests: assume role, run minimal allowed actions, validate logs and CloudTrail events
Step 3: If plan includes IAM changes, create a canary update on a single pilot account with 24h observation
Step 4: Approve and roll out gradually using staged CI job with pause points and automatic rollback on alert
Step 5: If drift is detected post-upgrade, run automated revert PR and notify stakeholders via incident channel
health_checks: Policy checksum: store canonical hash of policy JSON in state outputs and compare in periodic job
Unexpected-action alert: tfsec custom rule that surfaces wildcard actions when module input changes
Attachment audit: verify number of inline policies attached to roles does not exceed expected count
Session expiration validation: confirm ephemeral sessions are issued with <= configured TTL
Cross-account binding check: ensure external principals listed match allowlist for the customer
monitoring_alerts: high_drift_rate: fires when >3 customer role policies change outside module-managed PRs in 24h
ephemeral_token_error_rate: fires when bootstrap token issuance fails >5% over 15m
illegal_wildcards_detected: immediate P0 alert to security and infra when tfsec finds '*'
upgrade_plan_diffs: notify infra-owners when terraform plan for module shows destructive changes
